events.factual_description: Rhizome DC and Transparent Productions present Stephan Crump’s Passerine on Saturday, November 21, 2026. The official presenter page lists doors at 7:00 PM, music at 7:30 PM, and a $25-$30 sliding-scale face price. The quartet is Stephan Crump on acoustic bass, Ches Smith on percussion, Kenny Warren on trumpet, and David Leon on alto flute and saxophone. Crump’s official project page states that Passerine has been in development since fall 2024, is inspired by birds and different nest-building techniques, and releases its debut album on October 23, 2026 on Out of Your Head Records. Rhizome’s authorized Pools ticket page confirms the Washington, DC venue, the 7:00 PM doors / 7:30 PM music schedule, the $25-$30 sliding-scale face price, and current fee-inclusive totals of $27.75-$33.02.

enrichment.note: The exact Rhizome event page and its authorized Pools destination verify the date, venue, doors/music times, face-price range and quartet personnel. Passerine is not yet surfaced as an exact Apple Music album page in current search, so the exact Apple Music destination for Crump’s 2024 album Slow Water is used as the verified listening link rather than inventing a future catalog URL.

en.why_it_matters: Passerine has a clear compositional engine rather than a generic small-group premise: Crump is building the music around the different ways birds construct nests, and the quartet gives that idea an unusually open palette—acoustic bass, percussion, trumpet, alto flute and saxophone. With Ches Smith, Kenny Warren and David Leon, the draw is how four strong instrumental voices can turn a concrete natural-world idea into ensemble form and improvisation in Rhizome’s close room.
en.trip_verdict: If Saturday is open in the DMV, this is a good Rhizome night to choose, especially for a bass-led ensemble with unusual timbral balance and new music. I would not displace a stronger commitment or build a corridor trip around it.

es.why_it_matters: Passerine tiene un motor compositivo concreto y no la premisa genérica de otro cuarteto de jazz: Crump está construyendo la música a partir de las distintas maneras en que las aves hacen sus nidos, y la instrumentación abre un campo poco común —contrabajo, percusión, trompeta, flauta alto y saxofón. Con Ches Smith, Kenny Warren y David Leon, lo interesante es escuchar cómo cuatro identidades instrumentales fuertes convierten esa idea del mundo natural en forma de conjunto e improvisación dentro de una sala tan cercana como Rhizome.
es.trip_verdict: Si el sábado está libre en el DMV, es una buena noche para escoger Rhizome, sobre todo si quieres un ensamble liderado desde el bajo, con balance tímbrico poco común y música nueva. No desplazaría un compromiso más fuerte ni armaría un viaje por el corredor alrededor de esta fecha.
